forbidden.message: @Autowired injection: use constructor injection with final fields (a single constructor needs no annotation)
SecurityContextHolder outside <base>.api.security: inject the CurrentUser port instead
@Transactional belongs only on public methods of <base>.application services
new RestTemplate(): build a RestClient from the injected RestClient.Builder in <base>.infrastructure
Reading the system clock directly: inject java.time.Clock and call X.now(clock)
Empty catch block: handle, rethrow as a domain exception, or log with the exception
@CrossOrigin: CORS is configured once in the security config from validated properties
Wildcard CORS origin: list explicit origins from configuration
NoOpPasswordEncoder: hash passwords with BCrypt (strength >= 12) or Argon2
SQL built with String.format/formatted: use named parameters (:name) and .param(...)
JPA/Hibernate is not allowed unless the project profile declares it (then remove this rule from .claude/cuadrilla.json)
FetchType.EAGER: map associations LAZY and load them with an explicit fetch plan
Hibernate ddl-auto update/create: the schema changes only through Flyway migrations (use none or validate)
spring.jpa.open-in-view=true: keep it false and load what the response needs in the service
server.error.include-*: never expose stack traces or exception details to clients
Actuator exposure '*': expose only health (and info) over HTTP

recommendedSkills.why: Broad Spring Boot practices from GitHub's curated collection: constructor injection, typed configuration, DTOs, SLF4J, test slices.
recommendedSkills.conflicts: Ignore package-by-feature (cuadrilla uses package-by-layer: api/application/domain/infrastructure), Spring Data JPA as the default data layer (cuadrilla defaults to JdbcClient; JPA only if the profile declares it), @Transactional 'at the most granular level' anywhere (cuadrilla: application services only) and Spring profiles files carrying environment config with values (cuadrilla: env vars, no secrets in application-*.yml).

recommendedSkills.why: JUnit 5 structure, parameterized tests, @Nested grouping and Mockito basics.
recommendedSkills.conflicts: Use AssertJ (assertThat) rather than JUnit Assertions, prefer hand-written fakes for repositories over @Mock/@InjectMocks, never @TestMethodOrder for ordering-dependent tests, and @Disabled is not a way to get the build green.

recommendedSkills.why: Checklist-style Spring Security review: method security, validation, headers, rate limiting, dependency scanning.
recommendedSkills.conflicts: Ignore the hand-written OncePerRequestFilter that puts tokens into SecurityContextHolder (cuadrilla uses the oauth2 resource server JwtDecoder), hasRole('ADMIN') checks (cuadrilla: hasAuthority('<PERMISSION_CODE>')) and controllers returning DTOs or ResponseEntity without the ApiResponse envelope.
